title: Cover and sheaf criterion for the integer action topology
statement: Let C be a category with a coherent integer shift and J a precoverage such that every shift preserves and reflects J-covering presieves. Let D, its topology K, and the degree-zero inclusion j be the integer-action constructions of [lem-sf-integer-action-slice-equivalence]. A sieve S on j(X) is K-covering if and only if its inverse image under j covers in the Grothendieck topology generated by J. The inclusion j is continuous. A presheaf of types on D is a K-sheaf if and only if its restriction along j is a sheaf for the topology generated by J. This criterion does not require pullbacks in C.

source.place: Agent-formulated consequence of the existing integer-action slice normalization; Tag 00W0 motivates the group-action site, but does not assert this twisted generalization.

proof.text: Use the existing proved sieve pull-push identities and topology membership criterion from the slice normalization construction. They immediately give the covering equivalence.

To preserve compatibility, normalize the composite of two tested labelled arrows to the common target by the existing slice counit isomorphism. Equality of their degrees forces both resulting arrows to have degree zero. They are therefore images of base arrows, and the original compatible family applies. Cancel the presheaf map of the normalization isomorphism. Cover preservation and compatibility preservation imply continuity.

For the reverse sheaf implication, restrict a compatible family on a covering sieve to its base inverse image, and take the unique base amalgamation. For each labelled arrow use the same slice normalization; compatibility and injectivity of the presheaf map of its isomorphism show that the section amalgamates that arrow. Uniqueness is detected on degree-zero arrows. This works for empty categories and empty covering families.

lean.statement:
theorem integerActionTopologyCriterion
    (J : Precoverage C)
    (hcover : ∀ (n : ℤ) (X : C) (R : Presieve X),
      R ∈ J X ↔ R.map (shiftFunctor C n) ∈ J ((shiftFunctor C n).obj X)) :
    (∀ (X : C) (S : Sieve (IntegerActionSite.mk X : IntegerActionSite C)),
      S ∈ integerActionTopology J (IntegerActionSite.mk X) ↔
        S.functorPullback (integerActionInclusion (C := C)) ∈ J.toGrothendieck X) ∧
    (integerActionInclusion (C := C)).IsContinuous J.toGrothendieck
      (integerActionTopology J) ∧
    (∀ P : (IntegerActionSite C)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w,
      Presieve.IsSheaf (integerActionTopology J) P ↔
        Presieve.IsSheaf J.toGrothendieck
          ((integerActionInclusion (C := C)).op ⋙ P))
